Some basic plots for quality control

library(patchwork)
# Histogram for QUAL
p1=ggplot(fixed_data, aes(x = QUAL)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "blue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Variant Quality", x = "Quality (phred)", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

# Histogram for dp_data
p2=ggplot(fixed_data, aes(x = dp_data)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5, fill = "orange", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of variant read depth (DP)", x = "Depth", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_minimal()

p1+p2

MAGs

We load the MAG information for each contig

mag=read.table("../data/snps/S15.ctg2bins.txt",h=F)
colnames(mag)=c("MAG","CTG")
fixed_data=left_join(fixed_data,mag,by=c("CHROM"="CTG"))

#contig coverage
ccov=read.table("../data/snps/S15_bins.depth.mosdepth.summary.txt",h=T)
ccov=left_join(ccov,mag,by=c("chrom"="CTG"))
#we compute mag coverage
mag_cov=ccov %>% group_by(MAG) %>%summarize(l=sum(length),bases=sum(bases)) %>% mutate(mean_cov=bases/l)
#we compute number of mutations per MAG
mag_mut=fixed_data %>% group_by(MAG) %>% summarize(count=n())
#we join mag mut and cov
mag_mut_cov=left_join(mag_mut,mag_cov)
## Joining with `by = join_by(MAG)`
mag_mut_cov$mutations_per_megabase <- mag_mut_cov$count / (mag_mut_cov$l / 1e6)
#we plot mutations per megabase

#we load some mag stats from checkM result
mag_qual=read.delim("../data/MAG_SMAG/mags_mining_S15.tsv",header=T)
mag_qual$mag=paste0(mag_qual$mag_name,".",mag_qual$mag_id)
mag_qual=mag_qual %>% select(mag,phylum,class,order,completeness,contamination,strain_heterogeneity,genome_size,gc,N50)
mag_mut_cov_tax=left_join(mag_mut_cov,mag_qual, by=c("MAG"="mag"))

we build a linear model to check if variants can be explained by some variable

a=lm(data=mag_mut_cov_tax,log(mutations_per_megabase)~mean_cov+contamination+gc+strain_heterogeneity+completeness+phylum)
summary(a)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = log(mutations_per_megabase) ~ mean_cov + contamination + 
##     gc + strain_heterogeneity + completeness + phylum, data = mag_mut_cov_tax)
##

## phylumNitrospirota_A   -2.0527709  0.8455467  -2.428 0.020811 *  
## phylumProteobacteria   -2.1659095  0.5497183  -3.940 0.000399 ***
## ---

## F-statistic: 7.051 on 10 and 33 DF,  p-value: 8.325e-06
# we plot some interesting associations
# Fit a linear model
model <- lm(log(mutations_per_megabase) ~ strain_heterogeneity, data = mag_mut_cov_tax)

# Extract R-squared and p-value
r_squared <- summary(a)$r.squared
p_value <- summary(a)$coefficients[5, 4]

p1=ggplot(mag_mut_cov_tax, aes(x=strain_heterogeneity,y=log(mutations_per_megabase), color=phylum)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +  # Add points
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +  # Add linear model
  labs(
    title = "Mutations per Megabase vs Strain heterogeneity",
    x = "Strain heterogeneity",
    y = "Mutations per Megabase"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = max(mag_mut_cov_tax$strain_heterogeneity) * 0.7, y = max(log(mag_mut_cov_tax$mutations_per_megabase)), 
           label = paste0("R² = ", round(r_squared, 3), 
                          "\nP-value = ", signif(p_value, 3)), 
           color = "black", size = 5, hjust = 0) +
  theme_minimal()

# Fit a linear model
model <- lm(mutations_per_megabase ~ gc, data = mag_mut_cov_tax)

# Extract R-squared and p-value
r_squared <- summary(model)$r.squared
p_value <- summary(model)$coefficients[2, 4]

p2=ggplot(mag_mut_cov_tax, aes(x=gc,y=mutations_per_megabase, color=phylum)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +  # Add points
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +  # Add linear model
  labs(
    title = "Mutations per Megabase vs GC-content",
    x = "GC-content",
    y = "Mutations per Megabase"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = max(mag_mut_cov_tax$gc) * 0.7, y = max(mag_mut_cov_tax$mutations_per_megabase), 
           label = paste0("R² = ", round(r_squared, 3), 
                          "\nP-value = ", signif(p_value, 3)), 
           color = "black", size = 5, hjust = 0) +
  theme_minimal()


# Fit a linear model
model <- lm(mutations_per_megabase ~ mean_cov, data = mag_mut_cov_tax)

# Extract R-squared and p-value
r_squared <- summary(model)$r.squared
p_value <- summary(model)$coefficients[2, 4]

p3=ggplot(mag_mut_cov_tax, aes(x=mean_cov,y=mutations_per_megabase, color=phylum)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +  # Add points
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "blue", linetype = "dashed") +  # Add linear model
  labs(
    title = "Mutations per Megabase vs Genome Coverage",
    x = "Genome coverage",
    y = "Mutations per Megabase"
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = max(mag_mut_cov_tax$mean_cov) * 0.7, y = max(mag_mut_cov_tax$mutations_per_megabase), 
           label = paste0("R² = ", round(r_squared, 3), 
                          "\nP-value = ", signif(p_value, 3)), 
           color = "black", size = 5, hjust = 0) +
  theme_minimal()


(p1+p2+p3) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom")

Plot by phylum

library(ggplot2)

# Plot mutations per megabase by phylum
ggplot(mag_mut_cov_tax, aes(x = phylum, y = log(mutations_per_megabase), fill = phylum)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_y_log10() +  # Use log10 scale for better visualization if the range is wide
  labs(
    title = "Variants per Megabase by Phylum",
    x = "Phylum",
    y = "Variants per Megabase"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))  # Rotate x-axis labels

InStrain

WE use variants from InStrain caller using two ANI filters at 95% (default) and 97% (custom). It seem that the custom produce better results

d1=read.table(gzfile("../data/snps/InStrain/is_S15_def_SNVs.tsv.gz"),h=T,sep="\t")
#d1=d1 %>% filter(class == "SNV")
d2=read.table(gzfile("../data/snps/InStrain/is_S15_custom_SNVs.tsv.gz"),h=T,sep="\t")
#d2=d2 %>% filter(class == "SNV")

We filter for a minimum of read coverage >=5 for each allele

# Filter rows where both the reference and variant allele have at least 5 reads
filtered_d1 <- d1 %>%
  filter(ref_base %in% c("A", "C", "T", "G") &  # Ensure valid base
           con_base %in% c("A", "C", "T", "G") &
           var_base %in% c("A", "C", "T", "G") &
           (case_when(
              ref_base == "A" ~ A >= 5,
              ref_base == "C" ~ C >= 5,
              ref_base == "T" ~ T >= 5,
              ref_base == "G" ~ G >= 5,
              TRUE ~ FALSE
            )) &
           (case_when(
              var_base == "A" ~ A >= 5,
              var_base == "C" ~ C >= 5,
              var_base == "T" ~ T >= 5,
              var_base == "G" ~ G >= 5,
              TRUE ~ FALSE
            )))

# View the filtered data

We perform some analysis at MAG level, first we add the metadata

mag_mut_d1=filtered_d1 %>% group_by(MAG) %>% summarise(n=n()) %>% arrange(desc(n))
#we join mag mut and cov
mag_mut_cov_d1=left_join(mag_mut_d1,mag_cov)
## Joining with `by = join_by(MAG)`
mag_mut_cov_d1$mutations_per_megabase <- mag_mut_cov_d1$n / (mag_mut_cov_d1$l / 1e6)
mag_mut_cov_tax_d1=left_join(mag_mut_cov_d1,mag_qual, by=c("MAG"="mag"))

#custom
mag_mut_d2=filtered_d2 %>% group_by(MAG) %>% summarise(n=n()) %>% arrange(desc(n))
#we join mag mut and cov
mag_mut_cov_d2=left_join(mag_mut_d2,mag_cov)
## Joining with `by = join_by(MAG)`
mag_mut_cov_d2$mutations_per_megabase <- mag_mut_cov_d2$n / (mag_mut_cov_d2$l / 1e6)
mag_mut_cov_tax_d2=left_join(mag_mut_cov_d2,mag_qual, by=c("MAG"="mag"))
#library(patchwork)

data <- data.frame(
  Category = c(
    "Total mapped pairs",
    "Pairs passing max insert size threshold",
    "Pairs passing min insert size threshold",
    "Pairs passing mapQ threshold",
    "Pass min read ANI",

)

# Create the barplot

  coord_flip() +  # Flip the coordinates for a horizontal barplot
  labs(
    title = "Mapping and Filtering Metrics",
    x = "Category",
    y = "Percentage"
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(scale = 1)) +  # Show percentage on the y-axis

    legend.position = "none",

    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")
  )

# Histogram for QUAL
p1=ggplot(filtered_d1, aes(x = var_freq)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, fill = "blue", color = "black", alpha = 0.7) +

  labs(title = "Distribution of variant read depth (DP)", x = "Depth", y = "Frequency") +

  theme_minimal()

We build a linear model to test for association regarding the number of mutations

a=lm(data=mag_mut_cov_tax_d1,mutations_per_megabase~mean_cov+contamination+gc+strain_heterogeneity+completeness)
summary(a)
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = mutations_per_megabase ~ mean_cov + contamination + 
##     gc + strain_heterogeneity + completeness, data = mag_mut_cov_tax_d1)
## 
## Residuals:
##    Min     1Q Median     3Q    Max 
##  -4682  -2522  -1145   2054   9616 
## 
## Coefficients:
##                       Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)  
## (Intercept)          13715.851   7561.887   1.814   0.0776 .
## mean_cov                 4.617      2.551   1.810   0.0782 .
## contamination          -79.010    109.882  -0.719   0.4765  
## gc                     -33.036     69.651  -0.474   0.6380  
## strain_heterogeneity    41.265     25.183   1.639   0.1095  
## completeness           -90.240     64.026  -1.409   0.1668

Highly significant (p < 0.001). Each unit increase in mean_cov is associated with an increase of ~4.32 mutations per megabase

The model explains 31.6% of the variance in mutations_per_megabase.

mean_cov: The only significant predictor (p < 0.001). It has a strong, positive effect on mutation rates, meaning higher sequencing coverage results in more detected mutations. This aligns with the expectation that greater coverage improves variant detection sensitivity.

Other predictors (contamination, gc, strain_heterogeneity, completeness) are not statistically significant (p > 0.05), suggesting they do not have strong or consistent effects on mutation rates in this dataset.

# Count MAGs per phylum
phylum_counts <- table(mag_mut_cov_tax_d2$phylum)

# Filter phyla with at least 5 MAGs
valid_phyla <- names(phylum_counts[phylum_counts >= 5])
filtered_data <- mag_mut_cov_tax_d2[mag_mut_cov_tax_d2$phylum %in% valid_phyla, ]

anova_model <- aov(mutations_per_megabase ~ phylum, data = filtered_data)
summary(anova_model)
##             Df    Sum Sq Mean Sq F value Pr(>F)  
## phylum       2  16513378 8256689   2.481 0.0987 .
## Residuals   34 113139153 3327622                 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
tukey_results_filtered <- TukeyHSD(anova_model)
print(tukey_results_filtered)
##   Tukey multiple comparisons of means
##     95% family-wise confidence level
## 
## Fit: aov(formula = mutations_per_megabase ~ phylum, data = filtered_data)
## 
## $phylum
##                                        diff       lwr       upr     p adj
## Actinobacteriota-Acidobacteriota -1705.0196 -3774.241  364.2015 0.1229662
## Proteobacteria-Acidobacteriota   -1961.6114 -4269.924  346.7014 0.1086080
## Proteobacteria-Actinobacteriota   -256.5918 -1974.031 1460.8479 0.9289376
ggplot(filtered_data, aes(x = phylum, y = mutations_per_megabase, fill = phylum)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "Number of Mutations per Megabase by Phylum (Filtered)",
    x = "Phylum",
    y = "Mutations per Megabase"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

There is no strong evidence that the mean number of mutations per megabase differs significantly among the phyla included in the filtered dataset.
